\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ભૂલ} (bhūl)}{ભૂલ (bhūl)}]{\gu{ભૂલ} (bhūl) — a mistake}

\label{lesson:GU-C376-bhul}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to get done, then the Gujarati for to provide.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ભૂલ}}
\textbf{\gu{ભૂલ}} — \emph{bhūl} — \textquotedblleft{}a mistake\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{હિસાબમાં} \gu{એક} \gu{પણ} \gu{ભૂલ} \gu{હશે} \gu{તો} \gu{આખું} \gu{પરિણામ} \gu{ખોટું} \gu{આવશે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo hisābmā̃ ek paṇ bhūl haśe to ākhũ pariṇām khoṭũ āvśe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If there is even one mistake in the accounts, the whole result will come out wrong.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ભૂલ}} (\emph{bhūl}) shares its source with \textbf{\gu{ભૂલવું}} (\emph{bhūlvũ}), \textquotedblleft{}to forget\textquotedblright{}: CDIAL lists both under a reconstructed \emph{bhull}, \textquotedblleft{}err, forget\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9538).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhūl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhūl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo hisābmā̃ ek paṇ bhūl haśe to ākhũ pariṇām khoṭũ āvśe.} — If there is even one mistake in the accounts, the whole result will come out wrong.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to get done, then the Gujarati for to provide, then say \emph{bhūl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ભૂલ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A mistake\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ગફલત} (gaphlat)}{ગફલત (gaphlat)}]{\gu{ગફલત} (gaphlat) — negligence}

\label{lesson:GU-C376-gaphlat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to provide, then the Gujarati for a mistake.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ગફલત}}
\textbf{\gu{ગફલત}} — \emph{gaphlat} — \textquotedblleft{}negligence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{ડ્રાઈવર} \gu{ગફલત} \gu{કરશે} \gu{તો} \gu{ગાડી} \gu{ખાડામાં} \gu{પડશે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo ḍrāīvar gaphlat karśe to gāḍī khāḍāmā̃ paḍśe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the driver is careless, the car will end up in a ditch.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ગફલત}} (\emph{gaphlat}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ghaflat}, \textquotedblleft{}heedlessness\textquotedblright{}, through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gaphlat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gaphlat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo ḍrāīvar gaphlat karśe to gāḍī khāḍāmā̃ paḍśe.} — If the driver is careless, the car will end up in a ditch.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to provide, then the Gujarati for a mistake, then say \emph{gaphlat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ગફલત} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Negligence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ખામી} (khāmī)}{ખામી (khāmī)}]{\gu{ખામી} (khāmī) — a defect}

\label{lesson:GU-C376-khami}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a mistake, then the Gujarati for negligence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ખામી}}
\textbf{\gu{ખામી}} — \emph{khāmī} — \textquotedblleft{}a defect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{નવા} \gu{ફોનમાં} \gu{કોઈ} \gu{ખામી} \gu{હશે} \gu{તો} \gu{દુકાનદાર} \gu{તે} \gu{બદલી} \gu{આપશે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo navā phonmā̃ koī khāmī haśe to dukāndār te badlī āpśe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If there is a defect in the new phone, the shopkeeper will replace it.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ખામી}} (\emph{khāmī}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{khāmī}, \textquotedblleft{}rawness, a shortcoming\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khāmī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khāmī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo navā phonmā̃ koī khāmī haśe to dukāndār te badlī āpśe.} — If there is a defect in the new phone, the shopkeeper will replace it.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a mistake, then the Gujarati for negligence, then say \emph{khāmī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ઢીલ} (ḍhīl)}{ઢીલ (ḍhīl)}]{\gu{ઢીલ} (ḍhīl) — slackness; a delay}

\label{lesson:GU-C376-dhil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for negligence, then the Gujarati for a defect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ઢીલ}}
\textbf{\gu{ઢીલ}} — \emph{ḍhīl} — \textquotedblleft{}slackness; a delay\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{તમે} \gu{ઢીલ} \gu{કરશો} \gu{તો} \gu{ટ્રેન} \gu{છૂટી} \gu{જશે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo tame ḍhīl karśo to ṭren chūṭī jaśe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you dawdle, you will miss the train.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ઢીલ}} (\emph{ḍhīl}) CDIAL lists Gujarati \emph{ḍhīl}, \textquotedblleft{}loose, slack\textquotedblright{}, under a reconstructed \emph{ḍhila} (CDIAL 5590); \textquotedblleft{}a delay\textquotedblright{}, slack in doing a thing, is the noun's sense.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍhīl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍhīl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo tame ḍhīl karśo to ṭren chūṭī jaśe.} — If you dawdle, you will miss the train.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for negligence, then the Gujarati for a defect, then say \emph{ḍhīl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ઢીલ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Slackness; a delay\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{સુધરવું} (sudharvũ)}{સુધરવું (sudharvũ)}]{\gu{સુધરવું} (sudharvũ) — to get better}

\label{lesson:GU-C376-sudharvu-improve}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a defect, then the Gujarati for slackness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{સુધરવું}}
\textbf{\gu{સુધરવું}} — \emph{sudharvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to get better\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{તમે} \gu{રોજ} \gu{અભ્યાસ} \gu{કરશો} \gu{તો} \gu{તમારા} \gu{ગુણ} \gu{સુધરશે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo tame roj abhyās karśo to tamārā guṇ sudharśe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you study every day, your marks will improve.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \gu{તે} \gu{છોકરો} \gu{ઘણો} \gu{સુધર્યો}, \emph{te chokro ghaṇo sudharyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{સુધરવું}} (\emph{sudharvũ}) is the intransitive partner of \textbf{\gu{સુધારવું}} (\emph{sudhārvũ}), \textquotedblleft{}to mend\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists both under a reconstructed \emph{śuddhakāra}, \textquotedblleft{}making clean\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12521).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo tame roj abhyās karśo to tamārā guṇ sudharśe.} — If you study every day, your marks will improve.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a defect, then the Gujarati for slackness, then say \emph{sudharvũ} again
\end{itemize}
